cohort: Infants born at less than 1,500 g or less than 30 weeks gestational age who developed feeding intolerance (FI) and did not have congenital/chromosomal disorders, pre-existing thrombocytopenia/platelet transfusion, or history of bowel resection.
finding: Feeding intolerance (FI) caused by necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) or sepsis was associated with a decrease in platelets from baseline, lower platelet count, and higher immature-to-total neutrophil (I/T) ratio at the onset of FI, with the combination of a >=10% decrease in platelets and an I/T ratio >=0.1 showing high specificity (0.97) for diagnosis.
